reference.title: Dumbbell Half Kneeling Single Arm Shoulder Press (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the shoulder, breathe out as you press, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; tall-kneeling or standing single-arm press

cues.text: Kneel with the right knee down under the hip and the left foot flat in front, both knees about 90 degrees. Squeeze the right glute, ribs down. Dumbbell at the right shoulder, palm facing forward; left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight up, without leaning away from it.
Arm nearly straight, biceps by the ear, wrist stacked over the shoulder; trunk still tall.
Lower under control to the shoulder in about 2 s.
Brace again and repeat; switch sides (and knees) after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning away from the dumbbell or arching the low back
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the down-leg glute, keep the ribs down; use a lighter weight.

mistakes.mistake: Front knee caving in or the pelvis rotating
mistakes.fix: Keep the front shin vertical and the hips square to the front.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing out in front of the head
mistakes.fix: Finish with the dumbbell over the shoulder, biceps near the ear.
Start with the shoulder down and the elbow under the wrist.

kinematics.norm: Half-kneeling: down knee under the hip, front shin about vertical, both knees about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Upper arm about level at the bottom to about 160-170 degrees overhead (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees or more at the bottom (forearm vertical), nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)
Trunk stays vertical; a unilateral load raises oblique and back-stabilizer activity to resist side bending (Saeterbakken 2012; Trunk 2005)
Controlled, about 1.5 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1101612, Dumbbell Half Kneeling Single Arm Shoulder Press (male), video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
Trunk muscle electromyographic activity with unstable and unilateral exercises (J Strength Cond Res 19(1):193-201, 2005; PubMed 15705034)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Kneel on a mat or folded towel to protect the down knee.
The EMG studies used seated and standing presses; no study of the half-kneeling press itself was found.
modify: Knee discomfort: put a pad under the down knee, or do the press standing.
Shoulder pain overhead: press with the palm facing in (neutral grip) and stop short of full overhead.
regressions: Tall-kneeling (both knees down) or seated single-arm press.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover of the press; dumbbell presses gave higher anterior deltoid activity than barbell presses (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover of the press; dumbbell presses gave higher anterior deltoid activity than barbell presses (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the upper arm out and up; works hard through the press.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the upper arm out and up; works hard through the press.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow in the top half.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbow in the top half.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade so the arm can reach overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade so the arm can reach overhead.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Stop the trunk side-bending away from the one-sided load. A unilateral press gave much higher external oblique activity than a bilateral press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Stop the trunk side-bending away from the one-sided load. A unilateral press gave much higher external oblique activity than a bilateral press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk; the half-kneeling stance takes away help from the legs, so the trunk works more (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: The glute of the down leg squeezes to keep the hip extended and the pelvis level (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: The glute of the down leg squeezes to keep the hip extended and the pelvis level (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the trunk tall; a unilateral press activated the back stabilizers more than a bilateral press (Trunk 2005; Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the trunk tall; a unilateral press activated the back stabilizers more than a bilateral press (Trunk 2005; Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder as the arm rises.

guides.label: Press straight up over the shoulder
